source.description: NDMA wing mandates extracted from the mandate PDF chapters requested for SimExAI wing behavior.
required_wings: Technical Equipment & Maintenance Wing (Tech E & M)
Infrastructure Advisory and Project Development Wing (IA&PD)
Regional & Military Collaboration and Media Wing (RM & M)

technical_early_warning.name: Technical Early Warning Wing (Tech EW)
technical_early_warning.mandate_scope: Global and local hazard monitoring, 6-12 month forecasting, risk analysis, early warning dissemination, risk communication, and AI/GIS-enabled decision support for proactive disaster risk management.

pre_disaster: Develop and operate national early warning systems for hydro-meteorological, geological, climatic, and region-specific hazards.
Produce multi-hazard exposure and risk assessments using geospatial and meteorological datasets.
Integrate data streams from PMD, SUPARCO, WAPDA, PDMAs, line ministries, and global platforms.
Issue early warnings, alerts, advisories, and impact-based forecasts with relevant stakeholders.
Provide technical support for preparedness planning, scenario building, and regional or international simulation exercises.
Maintain disaster information systems, dashboards, and decision-support tools.
Build federal and provincial stakeholder capacity on early warning and risk analytics.
during_disaster: Monitor hazards, impacts, and evolving risk scenarios in real time using available technology platforms and portals.
Provide early warning updates and risk intelligence to decision-makers.
Support NEOC and response wings with situational analysis, maps, dashboards, and analytics.
Integrate field data, satellite imagery, and remote sensing for impact assessment and response prioritization.
Support inter-agency coordination with timely evidence-based risk and impact information.
post_disaster: Support damage, loss, and needs assessments using geospatial and analytical tools.
Analyze early warning performance and data gaps after the event.
Document lessons learned to improve forecasting models, thresholds, and dissemination mechanisms.
Enhance national disaster risk databases and historical hazard repositories.
Support early recovery and resilience planning through risk-informed analytics and modelling.

key_functions: Develop, operate, and continuously enhance national early warning and decision-support systems.
Collect, integrate, and analyze multi-hazard data from national and international sources.
Generate and disseminate impact-based early warnings, alerts, and advisories.
Provide real-time technical and analytical support to all NEOC wings during emergencies.
Create GIS products, dashboards, maps, and situational awareness tools for decision-making.
Coordinate with federal and provincial departments, PDMAs, research institutions, and development partners.
Support SimExs, drills, SOPs, guidelines, technical frameworks, and capacity-building on early warning systems.

d_day: Validate the hazard trigger and issue the first impact-based warning to NEOC and stakeholders.
Publish initial hazard, exposure, and risk maps for operational prioritization.
Fuse field, satellite, meteorological, and partner data into a common risk picture.
Brief response wings on immediate secondary hazard risks and uncertainty.
d_plus_30: Maintain real-time hazard monitoring and update risk intelligence as impacts evolve.
Refresh dashboards and maps with field reports, remote sensing, and partner datasets.
Identify emerging hotspots, access constraints, and cascading hazard risks.
Provide technical analytics for NEOC coordination and response prioritization.
d_plus_90: Support damage, loss, and needs assessments with geospatial analysis.
Assess early warning system performance, data gaps, and forecast accuracy.
Refine hazard and exposure layers for early recovery decisions.
Document lessons for model, threshold, and dissemination improvements.

nidm.name: National Institute of Disaster Management (NIDM)
nidm.mandate_scope: Capacity building, training, research, knowledge management, disaster archives, lessons learned, and institutional strengthening across the full disaster management cycle.

pre_disaster: Update national disaster archives and lessons learned.
Document and share national and international best practices.
Task academia, DRR societies, and think tanks for risk communication and responder preparedness.
Roll out standardized community-based training modules.
Prepare trained national volunteers in high-risk zones.
during_disaster: Monitor deployment and performance of trained volunteers and DRR societies.
Facilitate short-term placement of human resources at disaster sites.
Support coordination of relief, donations, and early recovery planning.
Provide technical inputs for real-time decision-making based on early warning and field evidence.
Engage national and international academia for rapid assessments where required.
post_disaster: Conduct rapid impact and damage analysis reviews.
Consolidate field feedback, lessons learned, and response evidence.
Identify priority research, training, and capacity gaps.
Issue implementation-focused guidance to national academic institutions.

key_functions: Develop annual Academia Best Practices Manuals using national and global disaster knowledge.
Bridge validated best practices with national and sub-national users.
Operate the NIDM Think Tank for DRR and resilience inputs.
Design localized training for communities, public institutions, military, and first responders.
Coordinate with DRR, Plans, and Operations and Logistic Wing for policy, preparedness, and operational coherence.
Maintain a trained volunteers database for rapid mobilization and capacity mapping.
Connect disaster training with national youth, volunteer, and civic engagement initiatives.
Promote academia-policy-practice linkages through universities and centres of excellence.

d_day: Activate observer, volunteer, and training coordination channels.
Identify immediate human resource and volunteer support gaps at incident sites.
Provide evidence-based inputs from early warning and field feedback.
Start live documentation of coordination, training, and decision bottlenecks.
d_plus_30: Track performance of trained volunteers and DRR society deployments.
Coordinate short-term technical human resources for priority disaster sites.
Engage academic partners for rapid field assessment support.
Capture lessons on relief coordination, donations, and early recovery planning.
d_plus_90: Consolidate field feedback into a mid-response learning note.
Identify urgent training gaps affecting relief, camp, or responder performance.
Support rapid impact and damage analysis reviews with academic inputs.
Issue targeted guidance to academic and volunteer networks.

tech_equipment_maintenance.name: Technical Equipment & Maintenance Wing (Tech E & M)
tech_equipment_maintenance.mandate_scope: Digital readiness, real-time data visualization, robust ICT infrastructure, public alert channels, SITREP systems, portals, network resilience, data backup, and maintenance of NDMA technical systems.

pre_disaster: Disseminate hazard projections and disaster early warnings through the NDMA website and mobile alert app.
Maintain a round-the-clock digital environment for domain experts.
Develop and publish coordination software systems as needs emerge.
Provide real-time visualization of disaster impacts through portals and NEOC command displays.
Issue alerts and advisories based on meteorological data and risk assessment.
Monitor and update SITREP portals for casualties, injuries, and livestock losses.
Generate automated reports with customizable filters for decision-making.
Ensure network resilience and backend support for NDMA hardware assets.
Provide customized and periodic data to other wings for damage and recovery needs assessment.
Optimize mobile app and website performance during disaster events.
Secure, archive, and back up disaster datasets, SITREPs, and response logs.
during_disaster: Keep NEOC technical systems, portals, networks, displays, mobile apps, and websites operational.
Maintain live dashboards, SITREP tools, and automated reporting for operational decisions.
Provide technical troubleshooting, data support, and ICT continuity for all wings.
Protect and back up disaster-related digital records and response logs.
post_disaster: Archive response datasets, SITREPs, and logs for analysis.
Evaluate system performance and technical gaps.
Repair, patch, and optimize platforms based on event behavior.
Support recovery needs assessment with technical data services.

key_functions: Lead NDMA ICT matters and mission-critical IT projects.
Digitize, automate, and modernize NDMA operations through technology.
Operate the Pak NDMA Disaster Alert Mobile App for real-time notifications and safety guidance.
Maintain secure NDMA web platforms with backups and departmental controls.
Create centralized dashboards for alerts, advisories, and safety messages.
Operate deployable Mobile Disaster Emergency Operations Centre capability.
Implement digital attendance, inventory, and asset maintenance systems.
Strengthen NDMA's technical backbone through secure networks, cloud storage, and real-time data systems.

d_day: Confirm NEOC connectivity, dashboard availability, and alert platform readiness.
Publish or support immediate digital alerts, SITREPs, and command centre displays.
Stabilize communication, portal, and backend services for all wings.
Begin secure backup of incident data and response logs.
d_plus_30: Maintain 24/7 ICT, portal, and network support for ongoing operations.
Repair or replace failed communication, dashboard, or field technical assets.
Update SITREP, inventory, and reporting tools as operational data changes.
Provide customized datasets to response, planning, and assessment teams.
d_plus_90: Audit system performance and close urgent technical gaps.
Support damage and recovery needs assessment with data exports and dashboards.
Patch, optimize, and secure platforms under sustained disaster workload.
Archive verified response logs and datasets for analysis.

drr.name: Disaster Risk Reduction Wing (DRR)
drr.mandate_scope: Risk-informed preparedness, anticipatory action, inclusive systems, policy coherence, and provincial coordination aligned with NDMP-2026 and National DRR Strategy 2025-2030.

pre_disaster: Monitor multi-hazard risk, exposure, and vulnerability with NEOC Tech, line ministries, PDMAs, SDMA, GBDMA, and community systems.
Strengthen institutional preparedness through inclusive planning, service readiness, guidance, SOPs, and minimum standards.
Operationalize anticipatory action through hazard and district-specific triggers and early action protocols.
Support inclusive last-mile dissemination of disaster early warnings to vulnerable populations.
Use Disaster Needs Calculator outputs and need-gap analyses for preparedness planning.
during_disaster: Identify protection, access, and inclusion gaps affecting vulnerable groups and family clusters.
Activate and monitor anticipatory and early actions where lead time exists or impacts are phased.
Provide policy oversight for consistent application of national DRR frameworks, SOPs, and coordination arrangements.
Use disaggregated data to guide equitable assistance and protection-sensitive action.
post_disaster: Conduct post-disaster assessments and learning reviews.
Review and refine anticipatory action triggers, protocols, and standard action packages.
Update DRR policies, SOPs, and minimum standards using evidence and lessons learned.
Integrate findings into preparedness, inclusion measures, and targeting tools.

key_functions: Formulate, coordinate, and oversee national DRR and anticipatory action frameworks.
Develop, update, and issue DRR policies, SOPs, and guidance notes.
Institutionalize anticipatory action through impact-based triggers, protocols, authorities, and coordination mechanisms.
Integrate gender, age, disability, and vulnerability considerations across preparedness, early warning, needs modelling, and response support.
Coordinate with NEOC Tech, PDMAs, SDMA, GBDMA, line ministries, UN agencies, INGOs, NGOs, and community networks.
Apply and refine needs assessment and modelling tools for equitable targeting and resource use.
Participate in SimExs and CISEs to test readiness, coordination, and early action systems.
Conduct post-disaster learning and accountability processes and fold lessons into policy systems.

d_day: Identify priority protection, access, and inclusion gaps from the initial impact picture.
Check whether anticipatory or early action triggers were met and activate standard action packages.
Advise NEOC on DRR policy, SOP, and vulnerable group implications.
Use disaggregated data to guide equitable response priorities.
d_plus_30: Monitor implementation of early actions and inclusion measures with provincial and district inputs.
Refine needs modelling and vulnerability analysis as field data improves.
Coordinate DRR guidance with line ministries, PDMAs, and community networks.
Escalate policy, access, and protection gaps affecting response delivery.
d_plus_90: Begin post-disaster learning review and assessment consolidation.
Review anticipatory action triggers, protocols, and targeting effectiveness.
Update guidance for safer relief sites, vulnerable groups, and equitable assistance.
Feed evidence into recovery planning and preparedness improvements.

infrastructure_advisory_project_developm.name: Infrastructure Advisory and Project Development Wing (IA&PD)
infrastructure_advisory_project_developm.mandate_scope: Technical advisories, audit frameworks, planning guidance, material hub coordination, infrastructure strengthening, rehabilitation, and resilient rebuilding before, during, and after disasters.

pre_disaster: Issue infrastructure awareness advisories for at-risk regions.
Establish infrastructure audit mechanisms to identify vulnerabilities.
Set up material hubs for rapid response capability in vulnerable areas.
Host national seminars on resilient infrastructure.
Evaluate international best practices for local adaptation.
Develop region-specific guidance for implementable designs.
Conduct cost estimation and damage projection for exposed structures.
during_disaster: Issue immediate infrastructure safety advisories linked with early warning.
Guide rapid infrastructure surveys through standard templates.
Provide technical input for temporary protective measures such as drainage clearance and barriers.
Facilitate release of materials from hubs under approved SOPs.
Support coordination with PDMAs and DDMAs through technical inputs.
post_disaster: Support rehabilitation of critical infrastructure using available stocks.
Support damage assessment and verification.
Provide technical assistance for debris removal.
Provide engineering support for temporary camp establishment.
Facilitate resilient reconstruction and rehabilitation using local resources.
Coordinate with line departments and provincial authorities for recovery operations.

key_functions: Prepare infrastructure advisories and technical guidelines.
Develop infrastructure audit frameworks and risk assessment tools.
Plan and coordinate material hubs.
Support damage assessment and data consolidation.
Guide resilient reconstruction and Build Back Better approaches.
Coordinate with PDMAs, line departments, donors, and stakeholders.
Promote local materials and cost-effective climate-resilient designs.

d_day: Issue immediate infrastructure safety guidance linked to the active warning.
Prioritize rapid surveys of critical facilities, lifelines, shelters, and access routes.
Advise on temporary protective measures and urgent material hub use.
Provide technical inputs to NEOC, PDMAs, and DDMAs for operational decisions.
d_plus_30: Run rapid infrastructure surveys using standard templates.
Verify damage reports and identify unsafe structures or routes.
Coordinate material release, temporary works, and engineering support for relief operations.
Consolidate infrastructure damage and risk data for planning.
d_plus_90: Support detailed damage assessment, verification, and cost estimation.
Advise on debris removal, temporary camps, and restoration priorities.
Develop resilient rehabilitation guidance for critical infrastructure.
Coordinate recovery technical inputs with line departments and provinces.

operations_logistic.name: Operations and Logistic Wing (Ops & Log)
operations_logistic.mandate_scope: Response, logistic support, recovery, and rehabilitation functions across pre-disaster preparedness, on-impact operations, and post-impact recovery in accordance with national policies, plans, strategies, and programmes.

pre_disaster: Prepare mid-term response and contingency plans.
Issue advisories and alerts.
Coordinate preparedness measures and simulation exercises.
Manage procurement, stocking, and international relief preparedness.
during_disaster: Lead national response, rescue, and evacuation coordination.
Conduct relief operations including needs, transportation, and distribution.
Establish relief and medical camps.
Manage emergency procurements and international relief or assistance.
post_disaster: Conduct needs assessment.
Manage ex-gratia assistance and compensation processes.
Coordinate foreign assistance.
Lead early recovery measures.

key_functions: Formulate, coordinate, and generate national response for any disaster.
Coordinate and liaise with federal and provincial ministries, departments, armed forces, rescue departments, and PDMAs.
Formulate response SOPs, guidelines, and contingency plans.
Participate in SimEx and CISE.
Issue advisories, alerts, SITREPs, situational updates, and operation progress reports.
Coordinate conferences, meetings, visits, briefs, and presentations on operations matters.
Coordinate aviation assets and required support.
Employ SAR assets within and outside the country.
Assess needs and coordinate logistic support requirements.
Provide ex-gratia assistance to disaster affectees.
Issue tax exemption certificates for relief item import or export by donors, UN agencies, INGOs, and NGOs.
Redress grievances.
Coordinate Recovery Needs Assessment with UN and government stakeholders during major disasters or international appeals.
Coordinate recovery and rehabilitation with INGOs and NGOs through Plans Wing.
Formulate, update, and implement national stocking policy.
Maintain national relief reserves and timely replenishment.
Oversee warehouse receipt, delivery, transportation, storage, security, and emergency action plans.
Coordinate relief receipts, distribution, allocation, re-allocation, and resource adjustment.

d_day: Activate national response, rescue, evacuation, and relief coordination.
Issue initial operational SITREP, priorities, and tasking for field response.
Coordinate aviation, SAR, armed forces, rescue departments, PDMAs, and line departments.
Start needs tracking, logistic support requests, and relief distribution planning.
d_plus_30: Sustain rescue, evacuation, relief distribution, camp, and medical support operations.
Coordinate transport, warehouses, relief receipts, and resource allocation.
Publish regular SITREPs and track operational gaps, grievances, and logistics constraints.
Coordinate emergency procurements and international relief support where required.
d_plus_90: Transition from emergency response to needs assessment and sustained relief.
Manage ex-gratia, compensation, and early recovery coordination inputs.
Oversee stock drawdown, distribution records, and replenishment needs.
Support Recovery Needs Assessment and recovery coordination with Plans Wing.

plans.name: Plans Wing
plans.mandate_scope: Preparedness planning, inter-agency coordination, INSaR readiness, needs analysis, resource mobilization, cluster planning, field deployment, donor engagement, and recovery planning across all phases.

pre_disaster: Preparedness and community readiness.
Coordination and inter-agency planning.
Search, rescue, and response readiness through INSaR.
Needs analysis and targeted interventions.
Resource mobilization and donor engagement.
Cluster and operational preparedness.
during_disaster: Activate clusters and field deployments.
Coordinate with government agencies.
Support relief and camp management.
Support INSaR operations.
Manage needs assessment and information management.
Mobilize resources and appeals.
post_disaster: Transition and handover responsibilities.
Consolidate data and lessons learned.
Support recovery and shelter.
Retain human resources and build capacity.
Support recovery needs and PDNA.
Sustain relief and resource flow.
Plan reconstruction and appeals.

key_functions: Lead multi-stakeholder preparedness planning with NGOs, INGOs, and INSaR.
Integrate NGO, INGO, UN, cluster, INSaR, NDMA, PDMA, DDMA, military, law enforcement, and local government plans.
Ensure INSaR readiness through equipment inspection, deployment planning, logistic support, and area control.
Activate contingency plans and support coordinated field operations under unified command.
Coordinate rapid needs assessments and track humanitarian gaps.
Share response data with authorities, clusters, and donors.
Engage donors and UN agencies for preparedness, response, and recovery.
Manage response-to-recovery transition, handovers, shelter rehabilitation, relief flow, PDNA, and recovery planning.
Recalibrate training, retain technical human resources, and integrate lessons learned.

d_day: Activate contingency plans, coordination platforms, clusters, and INSaR readiness checks.
Consolidate initial needs, humanitarian gaps, and field deployment priorities.
Coordinate with government, NGOs, INGOs, UN agencies, military, law enforcement, and local authorities.
Prepare donor, appeal, and resource mobilization inputs.
d_plus_30: Maintain cluster coordination, field deployment, relief, camp, and INSaR support.
Coordinate rapid needs assessments and information management.
Track resource gaps, donor inputs, and operational planning priorities.
Consolidate response data for authorities, clusters, and partners.
d_plus_90: Plan transition from response to recovery and handover responsibilities.
Support PDNA, recovery needs, shelter, and sustained relief planning.
Engage donors and UN agencies on reconstruction and recovery appeals.
Capture lessons affecting planning, coordination, and resource flow.

regional_military_media.name: Regional & Military Collaboration and Media Wing (RM & M)
regional_military_media.mandate_scope: Regional and military disaster collaboration, CISEs, liaison with partner countries and military components, global early warning dissemination, and national disaster risk communication through media and digital platforms.

pre_disaster: Maintain continuous liaison with disaster management bodies, regional organizations, and military components of friendly countries.
Sensitize partners about projected hazards.
Conduct CISE with partner countries and disaster management stakeholders.
Share post-exercise reports and lessons learned for proactive DRR.
Develop public risk communication and awareness strategies.
Disseminate early warning and preparedness messages.
Coordinate with ministries, media, and telecom operators on emergency communication protocols.
during_disaster: Share updated disaster early warnings with disaster management stakeholders.
Sensitize defence attaches and partners about the prevailing situation.
Share logistic demands when required.
Coordinate high-end equipment with partner countries.
Issue centralized real-time crisis communication.
Share safety instructions and evacuation advisories.
Coordinate messaging with NDMA, PDMAs, and responders.
Monitor and counter misinformation and maintain two-way communication with media and communities.
post_disaster: Share information with disaster management partners.
Coordinate additional support with Operations and Logistic Wing.
Coordinate sequential recovery of international support.
Assimilate realistic disaster data and conduct CISE after-action sharing.
Communicate damage, relief, and restoration updates.
Publicize government support and recovery measures.
Document NDMA response through media content.
Promote resilience and risk-informed recovery narratives.

key_functions: Coordinate and liaise with regional organizations, disaster management bodies, and military components of friendly countries.
Strengthen cooperation among nations and disaster response agencies.
Work out joint employment modalities between military components to reduce reaction time.
Build trust among Pakistan and partner-country disaster response teams.
Plan and conduct CISE.
Disseminate global disaster early warning advisories and alerts to regional bodies and military partners.
Coordinate bilateral and multilateral visits for proactive DRR.
Formulate and implement national disaster risk communication strategies.
Issue public advisories, alerts, media briefs, press releases, and situational communication products.
Monitor and manage disaster misinformation and disinformation.
Facilitate media coverage, senior leadership briefs, and disaster media archiving.

d_day: Notify regional, military, media, telecom, and partner-country coordination channels.
Issue the first unified public communication, safety instruction, and media line.
Coordinate military or partner high-end support requests with operational priorities.
Start misinformation monitoring and two-way media/community engagement.
d_plus_30: Maintain partner, regional, and military liaison on support needs and situation changes.
Coordinate centralized crisis communication with NDMA, PDMAs, responders, and media.
Share updated warnings, advisories, public safety content, and verified situation updates.
Track misinformation and correct false narratives quickly.
d_plus_90: Coordinate sequential recovery or redeployment of partner and military support.
Shift public communication toward relief access, restoration, and government support.
Document response evidence and partner contributions for institutional learning.
Prepare after-action inputs for CISE and partner reporting.

international_collaboration.name: International Collaboration Wing (IC)
international_collaboration.mandate_scope: International cooperation across pre-impact sensitization, on-impact need-gap analysis and assistance mobilization, and post-impact diplomatic liaison and recovery support.

pre_disaster: Sensitize and brief the international community on potential hazards.
Delineate high-level support required in case of major calamity.
Expand partnerships with international entities to enhance disaster resilience.
Prepare stakeholders for potential hazards through early warning systems and capacity-building initiatives.
during_disaster: Conduct rapid need-gap analysis to identify shortages in national resources, capabilities, and response mechanisms.
Map and track international resources from foreign governments and international organizations.
Align available international resources with identified national needs.
Mobilize pre-coordinated assistance through established agreements and networks.
post_disaster: Provide diplomatic liaison for affected foreign nationals with embassies for evacuation, medical aid, and repatriation.
Coordinate international funding, expertise, and resources for rehabilitation.
Support infrastructure rebuilding and long-term community resilience programs.

key_functions: Coordinate measures to address national resource gaps through international cooperation.
Liaise with federal ministries, including MoFA, and key stakeholders.
Keep the federal government and parliament updated on evolving situations.
Handover and manage logistical support.
Provide diplomatic support.
Engage Pakistani and foreign missions and diaspora communities.
Sensitize the global community on national and global hazards including avalanches, heatwaves, forest fires, cyclones, GLOF, landslides, floods, smog, and blizzards.
Promote risk resilience through international partnerships.

d_day: Assess immediate international assistance needs and national resource gaps.
Alert MoFA, foreign missions, diaspora channels, and international partners as required.
Map available international offers, agreements, and deployable support.
Brief federal stakeholders on international cooperation requirements and constraints.
d_plus_30: Mobilize pre-coordinated international assistance against validated gaps.
Track incoming offers, diplomatic clearances, handover, and logistic support requirements.
Coordinate with MoFA, missions, donors, and partner organizations.
Maintain federal and parliamentary situational updates on international support.
d_plus_90: Align international resources with relief, recovery, and rehabilitation priorities.
Coordinate diplomatic support for affected foreign nationals if needed.
Prepare international funding, expertise, and technical assistance options.
Document handover, use, and accountability of international assistance.
